summary:
[  edit  ]
The Serial  DAT  is used for serial communication through an external port, using the RS-232 protocol. These ports are usually a 9 pin connector, or a USB port on new machines.  (Using a USB port requires a USB-to-serial adapter and driver.)
All of a computer's available serial ports can be found in the Device Manager in the Windows operating system under Computer –> Manage -> Devices -> Serial… -> COM ports. Their names begin with 'COM'. Example: COM1, COM2, COM3.
To send bytes out this connection, see the send methods in the  serialDAT_Class , or in  Tscript  the  send  Command.
See also  Arduino  and  Serial CHOP .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: This check box enables the serial connection.

parameters.label: Row/ Callback  Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Interpret the incoming data as binary or ASCII data. If the format is Per Byte, one row is appended for each binary byte received. If the format is Per Line, one row is appended for each null or newline delimited message received.

parameters.label: One Per Byte
parameters.name: perbyte
parameters.description: (formerly called 'binary').

parameters.label: One Per Line
parameters.name: perline
parameters.description: (formerly called 'Ascii') null/newln delimited.

parameters.label: One Per Message
parameters.name: permessage
parameters.description: Full incoming msg.

parameters.label: Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Selects the COM port that the serial connection will use.  Default port names 1 through 8 are available in the popup menu, though any name can be manually entered in this field.

parameters.label: Baud Rate
parameters.name: baudrate
parameters.description: ⊞  - The maximum number of bits of information, including "control" bits, that are transmitted per second. Check your input device's default baud rate and set accordingly.

parameters.label: Data Bits
parameters.name: databits
parameters.description: ⊞  - This parameter sets the number of data bits sent in each. Data bits are transmitted "backwards". Backwards refers to the order of transmission, which is from least significant bit (LSB) to most significant bit (MSB). To interpret the data bits, you must read from right to left.

parameters.label: Parity
parameters.name: parity
parameters.description: ⊞  - This parameter can be set to none, even, or odd. The optional parity bit follows the data bits and is included as a simple means of error checking. Parity bits work by specifying ahead of time whether the parity of the transmission is to be even or odd. If the parity is set to be odd, the transmitter will then set the parity bit in such a way as to make an odd number of 1's among the data bits and the parity bit.

parameters.label: Stop Bits
parameters.name: stopbits
parameters.description: ⊞  - The last part of transmission packet consists of 1 or 2 Stop bits. The connection will now wait for the next Start bit.

parameters.label: DTR
parameters.name: dtr
parameters.description: ⊞  - The DTR (data-terminal-ready) flow control. (Windows Only).
